title: Level 4 (Expert) - A-14
notes:
West leads a club against 6NT. There are 11 top tricks (3 spade tricks, the ♥A, 3 diamond tricks, and 4 club tricks). A twelfth trick will be available if either the defensive spades or diamonds break 3-3.

South can also come to a twelfth trick with a squeeze if either defender has length in both spades and diamonds. The squeeze will be a simple 2 suit squeeze. A squeeze of this type can only mature when declarer has all of the tricks except for 1. As South starts with 2 losers it is necessary for South to rectify the count.

Rectifying the count involves deliberately losing 1 or more tricks in order to correct the loser count for a squeeze. After winning the club lead, South should duck a heart trick, reducing his loser count to 1.

South can win any return and cash dummy's diamonds. If diamonds prove to be 3-3, South has his twelfth trick. When one of the opponents has 4 or more diamonds, South runs his heart and club winners. A heart is pitched from North on the last club winner. If East has a spade stopper as well as his known diamond guard, he will be forced to surrender a trick with his discard.

If West had started with guards in both spades and diamonds, the squeeze will operate with equal effectiveness. West will be squeezed on the play of the ♣A.

Nothing will be lost by playing this way if spades were always 3-3. If South's fourth diamond isn't good after the ♥A and clubs are cashed, South tries the spades and hopes for the best.
